doc.title: Rashied Ali and Henry Grimes interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, January 30, 2009

title: Recording dates, Konitz, Mulligan and no-piano groups
summary: Grimes recalls recording with Lee Konitz and playing with Mulligan and Dave Bailey as a sideman.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Well what was the recording dates like at that time. You showed up. Did you rehearse for them? And how long did you usually get in a record date?
I don’t know. I know I did some record dates but certain things I haven’t reckoned with yet and I don’t really remember. Are you talking about rhythm & blues groups?
No, no I’m talking about early on when you got into the jazz thing. It looks like you started recording like pretty actively, about once a month, around 1957.

Yeah I think Lee Konitz — I did some recording with him. But the rest of them, well they weren’t recording dates. I was just playing with them, like Gerry Mulligan and Lee Konitz and Dave Bailey, the drummer from —
And a lot of them. Just about all of them in that circle.
Was it different to play with Gerry Mulligan? He had no piano. Did that change your playing?

No that may be rare, I wanted to do more. But it was a lot of, at that time it was a lot of no piano playing, that I was doing, but I also did a lot of other groups. Like you say, Shafi Hadi was one of the sidemen, you know, same as I was. I was a sideman then.
